title: Grave search — Broadford Cemetery Trust (draft)
metaDescription: Search Broadford Cemetery's burial records by name or plot, see where each grave is on a map of the grounds, and find photos and stories.

header.heading: Grave search
header.lead: Search the Trust’s burial records by name or plot and see exactly where a grave sits in the grounds. Zoom in on the map to read the names on each plot.

notFound.label: If you cannot find the name you are looking for
notFound.body:
Most of the Cemetery’s records were lost in the 1950s. A grave may exist here even though we have no record of it — and an old map recovered a few years ago has since helped us identify a number of unmarked graves.

If a search finds nothing, it is worth trying these before giving up:

  • Search the surname only, with no given name.
  • Try spelling variants. Nineteenth-century clerks were inconsistent, and names were often anglicised.
  • Check whether the burial may have been at another cemetery in the district.

The Trust may still be able to help. Please contact us at broadfordct@gmail.com with whatever you know — a name, an approximate year, a relationship — and a trustee will look into it. Enquiries like these also help us improve the records.

sideNotices.label: Before you visit
sideNotices.body: Write down or photograph the section and plot reference before you leave home. Mobile coverage at the cemetery is not guaranteed.

sideNotices.label: About the records
sideNotices.body: The interment records and plot map are kept by the Broadford Cemetery Trust. About 2,100 plots and 2,100 burials are recorded. Some burials are known only from death certificates, so their place in the grounds is not certain.

sideNotices.label: Researching a family history
sideNotices.body: Because most of the pre-1950s records were lost, a search may find nothing even where a burial certainly took place. The History page explains what happened to the records.

story.lead: Tell us about someone buried at Broadford Cemetery, or send a photo of their headstone. A trustee reads every story before it appears on the website.
